title: Force and motion - 123 school
heading: Force and motion
intro: All the data you need is in the question. Round to the correct number of digits.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of speed?
Convert 20 m/s to km/h.
Convert 54 km/h to m/s.
Which formula applies to speed when the speed is constant?
A cyclist travels at 5.0 m/s. How far does he get in 12 s?
A runner runs 150 m at a speed of 6.0 m/s. How long does it take?
A walker covers 3.0 km in 20 minutes. What is his average speed in km/h?
A car travels 60 km in 1.0 hour and then 100 km in 1.0 hour. What is the average speed?
What do you see in a (s,t) graph with a horizontal line?

answers.b: The object moves at constant speed

questions.question: What does a straight, sloping upward line in a (s,t) graph mean?
What does a horizontal line in a (v,t) graph mean?
What does a straight, sloping upward line in a (v,t) graph mean?
How do you find the distance travelled from a (v,t) graph?

answers.a: From the area under the graph
answers.b: By the height of the graph
answers.c: By the slope of the graph
answers.d: By the lowest point of the graph

questions.question: In a (v,t) graph the speed is constant at 10 m/s for 6.0 s. How far does the object travel?
What is the SI unit of acceleration?
A car accelerates from 0 to 20 m/s in 8.0 s. What is the average acceleration?
A car brakes from 25 m/s to a standstill in 5.0 s. What is the deceleration?
A 1200 kg car accelerates at 2.0 m/s<sup>2</sup>. What is the resultant force?
A resultant force of 300 N gives an object an acceleration of 1.5 m/s<sup>2</sup>. What is the mass?
A resultant force of 50 N acts on a 10 kg cart. What is the acceleration?
What happens to an object when the resultant force is 0 N?

answers.b: It stays at rest or moves at constant speed

questions.question: The driving force of a car is 500 N and the friction force is also 500 N. What kind of motion does the car make?
The driving force is 800 N and the friction force is 300 N. What is the resultant force?

answers.b: 1100 N in the direction of travel
answers.c: 500 N in the direction of travel
answers.d: 500 N opposite to the direction of travel

questions.question: What does Newton's third law (action and reaction) state?

answers.a: The force you exert is greater than the reaction force
answers.b: The reaction force acts in the same direction as the action force
answers.c: A force always acts on one object and has no opposing force
answers.d: Two objects exert forces of equal size and opposite direction on each other

questions.question: You push a crate 5.0 m forward with a force of 40 N. How much work do you do? (W = F × s)
Lifting an object over 6.0 m takes 300 J of work. What is the force?
A driver travels at 20 m/s and has a reaction time of 0.75 s. What is the reaction distance?
The reaction distance is 14 m and the braking distance is 26 m. What is the stopping distance?
A car travels twice as fast. What happens to the braking distance?

answers.a: The braking distance becomes about 4 times as large
answers.c: The braking distance becomes 2 times as large
answers.d: The braking distance stays the same

questions.question: A stone falls without air resistance. The acceleration of free fall is 9.8 m/s<sup>2</sup>. What is the speed after 2.0 s?
A parachutist descends at constant speed. Which statement is correct?

answers.a: The force of gravity is equal to the air resistance
answers.b: Gravity is greater than air resistance
answers.c: Air resistance is greater than gravity

questions.question: Why do you slide forward when a car suddenly brakes?

answers.a: Because the car gives you a push
answers.c: Because of inertia you keep moving at the same speed
answers.d: Because the seat belt pulls you forwards

questions.question: Why does a crumple zone reduce the force on the occupants in a collision?

answers.a: The car brakes over a shorter time
answers.b: The car slows down over a longer time, so the deceleration is smaller
answers.c: The speed at the collision is lower
